conflicts.title: Med Script promises food stamps, Flex-card, and Social Security cash back
conflicts.detail: The Med Script says callers may qualify for 'increasing foods-stamp', a 'Flex-card', dental, vision, and 'cashback like add more money back into your pocket from Social Security check each month'. The Medicare Advantage training materials do not support food-stamp increases or Social Security cash back; these are not standard MA benefits and may be misleading.
conflicts.resolution: Excluded from Tressa's approved claims. Tressa may describe only documented MA supplemental benefits (dental, vision, hearing, fitness, OTC, transportation, care coordination) as plan-dependent, and must route specific benefit questions to a licensed agent.

conflicts.title: Med Script opening lacks required disclosures
conflicts.detail: The script opens with 'My name is Brain from US health care' and asks about Medicare A/B. It does not include licensed/agency identification, recording consent, non-affiliation, or the TPMO disclaimer required by the call-center training.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa uses the compliant opening from the call-center training before the script's purpose/qualification steps. She identifies herself as an AI assistant, not a licensed agent.

conflicts.title: Med Script discusses benefits before documenting the SOA
conflicts.detail: The script moves from A/B confirmation into a benefits pitch without a Scope of Appointment. The training requires the SOA before any plan-specific discussion.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa inserts a documented SOA step immediately after the opening/purpose and before benefits or plan discussion.

conflicts.title: Med Script asks for date of birth early
conflicts.detail: The script asks for date of birth before the name/ZIP and before any privacy explanation. The training says to protect privacy and verify identity only later, as needed.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa asks DOB only when needed for qualification, explains why, minimizes collection, and never requests SSN/bank/Medicare ID. Callers may decline.

conflicts.title: Script assumes a licensed human agent; Tressa is an AI
conflicts.detail: The training opening says 'licensed insurance agent' and the script transfers to a licensed agent. Tressa is an AI voice assistant and must not claim to be licensed or to be a human.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa discloses that she is an AI assistant and transfers plan-specific/enrollment questions to a licensed human agent after consent.

conflicts.title: TPMO carrier list and count are not provided
conflicts.detail: The training requires the TPMO disclaimer to state the number/list of organizations represented and that not every plan in the area is offered. The attachments do not specify the carrier list or count, and the script does not include a TPMO disclosure.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa uses a compliant placeholder that states she represents the plan options available through US Health Care and does not offer every plan in the area. The exact carrier list/count must be configured by an administrator before deployment.

conflicts.title: No plan-specific premiums, copays, networks, or formularies
conflicts.detail: The attachments are training material, not a carrier plan catalog. They contain general 2026 figures and typical benefits, but no plan-specific data for a ZIP code.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa never quotes plan-specific numbers. She explains general trade-offs and transfers to a licensed agent with verified plan data.

conflicts.title: MOOP figure is labeled 2025 in the quiz and 2026 in the comparison slide
conflicts.detail: The MA quiz says the 2025 in-network MOOP maximum was approximately $9,350. The Supplement vs Advantage slide (2026) also says 'Max up to $9,350 in-network'. The figure is training-era and may be outdated or plan-specific.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa does not quote the MOOP as a current fact. She says plans have an annual out-of-pocket maximum and a licensed agent can confirm the current plan-specific amount.

conflicts.title: Script asks age, but Medicare eligibility is not only age 65+
conflicts.detail: The script asks 'how old are you?' after the benefits pitch. Medicare also covers some people under 65 with disability, ESRD, or ALS. The attachments do not define a campaign age cutoff beyond general Medicare eligibility.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa asks age for campaign records but does not deny eligibility solely on age; she confirms Part A/B and plan rules and routes uncertain cases to a licensed agent.

conflicts.title: Lead source and prior express permission are not documented
conflicts.detail: The Med Script is an outbound-style call, but the attachments do not show documented prior permission or the lead source. The training prohibits cold calling and unpermitted lists.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa confirms permission at the opening and honors refusals/do-not-call requests. The campaign must supply documented consent before any outbound dialing; this is an open admin/compliance action.

conflicts.title: Script says 'Brain' (likely 'Brian') and 'US health care'
conflicts.detail: The greeting literally reads 'My name is Brain from US health care'. The script quiz treats that exact wording as the correct answer. 'Brain' is almost certainly a typo for 'Brian', and the agency name is inconsistently capitalized.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa uses her configured name (Tressa) and the approved agency name. Flagged for the script owner to correct the source; do not reproduce the typo.

conflicts.title: Script disclaimer is not a recording consent or TPMO disclosure
conflicts.detail: The script's 'short disclaimer' is a broad contact consent/hold-harmless paragraph, not the training-required recording consent, non-affiliation, or TPMO disclosure.
conflicts.resolution: Tressa delivers the required recording, non-affiliation, and TPMO disclosures at the opening, and keeps any contact consent accurate and separate. Legal review is required before using the script's hold-harmless language.

WELCOME ABOARD
Medicare Advantage
New Hire Agent Orientation
Your guide to starting strong as a Medicare Advantage agent.
Compliance • Product Knowledge • Client Success
Speaker notes: 1

What is Medicare Advantage?
Medicare Advantage (Part C) is a private health plan alternative to Original Medicare (Parts A & B). These plans are offered by private insurance companies approved by Medicare and must cover everything Original Medicare covers — often with extra benefits.
Private Plans
Offered by Medicare-approved private insurers
All-in-One
Combines Part A, Part B, and usually Part D
Extra Benefits
Dental, vision, hearing, fitness & more
Speaker notes: 2

Original Medicare vs. Medicare Advantage
Original Medicare
Part A (Hospital) + Part B (Medical)
No referral needed for specialists
Nationwide provider access
No out-of-pocket maximum
Optional Medigap + Part D
Higher flexibility, potentially higher costs
Medicare Advantage
All-in-one private plan (A + B + usually D)
Often requires network / referrals
Network-based (with some exceptions)
Annual out-of-pocket maximum
Extra benefits included
Lower predictability, more benefits
Speaker notes: 3

Key Benefits Agents Should Highlight
Dental & Vision
Preventive and comprehensive coverage often included
Hearing Aids
Coverage for hearing exams and devices
Fitness Programs
Gym memberships (e.g., SilverSneakers)
OTC Allowance
Monthly or quarterly over-the-counter benefits
Transportation
Rides to medical appointments
Care Coordination
Case management and wellness programs

MEDICARE AGENT
Call Center Training Script
Compliant Sales & Enrollment Call Framework
CMS-Aligned • Needs-Based • Professional
For licensed agents handling Medicare Advantage, Part D & related products
Speaker notes: 1

Training Agenda
Training Objectives
What agents will master
Core Compliance Rules
CMS requirements that protect you and the beneficiary
Call Flow Overview
7-step structure from greeting to close
Opening & Disclosures

Speaker notes: 2

Learning Objectives
By the end of this training, agents will be able to:
Deliver all required CMS disclosures accurately and early in the call
Complete a valid Scope of Appointment before discussing any specific plans
Verify eligibility and identity while protecting privacy (HIPAA)
Conduct effective needs discovery focused on doctors, meds, and priorities
Present plan options factually without steering or high-pressure tactics
Handle common objections professionally and close or schedule appropriately
Speaker notes: 3

Core Compliance Rules
Non-negotiable requirements for every marketing / sales / enrollment call
Identify Fully
State full name, licensed agent status, agency name. Disclose you are not affiliated with Medicare or the government.
Recording Consent
Advise the call is being recorded and obtain clear verbal permission before continuing.
TPMO Disclaimer
Deliver the required disclaimer about the number of organizations / plans you represent before discussing benefits.
Scope of Appointment
Document product types the beneficiary wants to discuss before any plan-specific conversation.
No Cold Calling
Only contact beneficiaries with documented prior permission. Never use purchased lists without consent.
No Pressure Language
Avoid “best,” “free,” false urgency, or any implication of government endorsement.

chunks.text:
Step 1 — Opening & Required Disclosures
SAMPLE SCRIPT
“Hello, may I speak with [Prospect Name]?
Hi [Name], this is [Your Full Name], a licensed insurance agent with [Agency Name]. This call may be recorded for quality assurance and compliance purposes. Do I have your permission to continue and record this conversation?
[Wait for clear yes.]
Thank you. I am calling regarding Medicare plan options. I represent [list carriers / number of organizations]. I am not connected with or endorsed by the federal government or the Medicare program. Is it okay to proceed?”
Speaker notes: 6

Step 2 — Scope of Appointment (SOA)
Must be completed and documented before any plan-specific discussion.
SAMPLE SOA LANGUAGE
“Before we discuss any specific plans, I need to document the types of products you would like to review today. This is called a Scope of Appointment.
Would you like to discuss Medicare Advantage plans, Medicare Supplement plans, Part D Prescription Drug plans, or a combination?
Please note that the products we discuss today will be limited to what you authorize right now. You are under no obligation to enroll in anything.”
Limit Scope
Stay strictly within the product types authorized.
Document It
Verbal or electronic record is required.
No Obligation
Always remind the beneficiary there is no pressure to enroll.
Speaker notes: 7

Medicare Status

Service Area

chunks.text:
Step 4 — Needs Discovery
Listen more than you talk. These questions uncover what truly matters.
Current Coverage
What type of coverage do you have now? (Original + Supplement, MA, Part D, etc.)
Satisfaction
How happy are you with your current plan? Any costs, coverage gaps, or access issues?
Providers
Which doctors, specialists, or hospitals are most important for you to keep?
Medications
What prescription medications do you take regularly?
Priorities
What matters most — lower premiums, predictable costs, dental/vision, broader network?
Upcoming Needs
Any upcoming procedures or expected changes in health needs?

chunks.text:
Steps 5–7 — Recap, Present, Close
5. Recap
• Summarize doctors, meds, priorities, and budget concerns
• Ask: “Did I get that right? Anything missing?”
• Builds trust and prevents mis-matches
6. Present Options
• Stay within the SOA products only
• Present 1–3 relevant options factually
• State trade-offs clearly (network, prior auth, costs)
• Remind: “I do not offer every plan in your area”
7. Close / Next Steps
• If ready: confirm understanding, complete enrollment
• If not: offer summary + schedule follow-up
• Never pressure same-call enrollment
• End with contact info + Medicare.gov / 1-800-MEDICARE

Key Knowledge Agents Must Master
Parts of Medicare
• A – Hospital Insurance
• B – Medical Insurance
• C – Medicare Advantage
• D – Prescription Drugs
• Medigap – Supplements Original
Main Enrollment Periods
• IEP – around 65th birthday
• AEP – Oct 15 to Dec 7
• MA OEP – Jan 1 to Mar 31
• SEPs – qualifying life events
Original vs Advantage
• Original: any provider accepting Medicare
• Advantage: network, often extra benefits
• Advantage has annual OOP max
• Trade-offs must be stated clearly
Always Offer Alternatives
• Medicare.gov
• 1-800-MEDICARE
• Local SHIP counselor
• Independent comparison tools

Practice these live with a partner or supervisor. Score for compliance + discovery quality.
AEP Inbound – Original Medicare
Caller wants lower drug costs and is open to comparing Advantage plans.

Member is unhappy with specialist access and considering a switch.

Remember
Compliance protects everyone.
Your job is to educate, listen, and help the beneficiary make an informed choice — never to push a plan.
Always use current carrier materials and have your compliance team review scripts before use.
Questions? Practice with your supervisor today.

ELIGIBILITY
Who Qualifies for Medicare?
You must generally be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident who has lived in the U.S. for at least 5 years.
Primary Pathways
Age 65 or Older
Most common path. Automatic enrollment if already receiving Social Security benefits.
Disability
Under 65 and entitled to Social Security disability benefits for 24 months (waiting period may be waived).
ESRD
Any age with permanent kidney failure requiring dialysis or a kidney transplant.
ALS (Lou Gehrig's)
Any age diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis — no waiting period.
Premium-Free Part A
Most people get Part A at no monthly cost if they (or a spouse) paid Medicare taxes for at least 10 years (40 quarters) while working.
Key Notes
• Part B is optional but most people enroll
• You can buy Part A if you do not qualify for free coverage
• Enrollment is not always automatic — check your situation
• Spousal work history can help you qualify

PART D
Prescription Drug Coverage
Optional coverage for outpatient prescription drugs. Available as a standalone plan or through most Medicare Advantage plans.
How It Works
Private insurance companies offer plans that follow Medicare rules. You pay a monthly premium and share costs for drugs.
Formulary
Each plan has a list of covered drugs (formulary). Check that your medications are covered before enrolling.
2026 OOP Cap
Thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act, out-of-pocket drug spending is capped at $2,100 in 2026.
Extra Help (LIS)
People with limited income and resources may qualify for the Low-Income Subsidy, which lowers premiums and costs.

FILLING THE GAPS
Medigap, Medicaid & Extra Help
Original Medicare leaves cost-sharing gaps. Several programs can reduce what you pay.
Medigap (Medicare Supplement)
Private policies that help pay deductibles, coinsurance, and copayments under Original Medicare. Standardized plans (A–N). Best bought during the 6-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period starting when Part B begins.
Medicaid / Dual Eligibility
State-federal program for people with limited income and resources. Dual eligibles can get help with Medicare premiums and cost-sharing, plus extra benefits such as long-term care and transportation.
Medicare Savings Programs
State programs that help pay Part A and/or Part B premiums and sometimes deductibles and coinsurance for people with modest income and resources.
Extra Help (Low-Income Subsidy)
Federal program that helps pay Part D premiums, deductibles, and copayments. Expanded eligibility under recent legislation. Apply through Social Security.
Speaker notes: 9

GETTING STARTED
Enrollment Periods & Key Decisions
Timing matters. Missing your initial enrollment window can result in lifelong late-enrollment penalties.
Initial Enrollment Period
• 7-month window around 65th birthday
• 3 months before + month of + 3 after
• Best time to avoid penalties
• Sign up for A and/or B
Annual Election Period
• Oct 15 – Dec 7 every year
• Switch between Original & Advantage
• Change or join Part D plans
• Changes take effect Jan 1
Special Enrollment
• Still working past 65 with employer coverage
• Moving, losing other coverage
• Qualifying life events
• Avoids late-enrollment penalties
Speaker notes: 10

SUMMARY
Key Takeaways
Remember these essentials when navigating Medicare.
Four Parts
A (Hospital), B (Medical), C (Advantage), D (Drugs). Understand what each covers before choosing.
Two Main Paths
Original Medicare + optional Medigap/Part D, or a Medicare Advantage plan that bundles coverage.
Costs Are Shared
Premiums, deductibles, and coinsurance apply. 2026 standard Part B premium is $202.90; Part A is free for most.
Help Is Available
Extra Help, Medicare Savings Programs, Medicaid, and Medigap can significantly lower your out-of-pocket costs.
Timing Matters
Enroll during your Initial Enrollment Period to avoid permanent late penalties. Review coverage every year.
Official Sources
Always verify details at Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE. Plans and costs change annually.

Question: Can Medicare Advantage plans charge higher cost-sharing than Original Medicare for the same service?
Options: A. Yes, without any limits; B. No, never; C. They must follow CMS rules and cannot exceed certain limits; overall value must be actuarially equivalent or better; D. Only for Part D drugs
Correct answer: C — Plans must provide at least the same overall value; individual services have cost-sharing limits set by CMS.

chunks.section: Quiz Q31: What is the Medicare Advantage Maximum Out-of-Pocket (MOOP) designed to do?
chunks.text:
Question: What is the Medicare Advantage Maximum Out-of-Pocket (MOOP) designed to do?
Options: A. Limit the plan’s payments to providers; B. Protect enrollees by capping their annual spending on covered Part A and B services; C. Replace the Part B deductible; D. Apply only to prescription drugs
Correct answer: B — MOOP protects beneficiaries by limiting their annual out-of-pocket costs for covered services.

Correct answer: B — The MA OEP (January–March) allows one change for those already in MA.

Correct answer: B — CMS Star Ratings measure quality; higher-rated plans may receive bonus payments and attract more members.

chunks.section: Quiz Q34: True or False: All Medicare Advantage plans must cover the same core benefits as

Options: A. True; B. False – they can exclude hospital care; C. False – they only cover Part B; D. True, but only if the member pays extra
Correct answer: A — MA plans must cover all medically necessary Part A and Part B services (with limited exceptions such as hospice).

Correct answer: B — The best choice depends on doctors/hospitals used, expected care needs, travel, and total cost exposure.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Source priority: (1) mandatory CMS/Medicare legal and compliance requirements; (2) Medicare Agent Call Center Training — the compliant call flow and required disclosures; (3) Medicare Advantage New Hire Orientation — MA compliance rules; (4) Medicare Basics Overview and MA quiz — product facts; (5) Supplement vs Advantage comparison; (6) the campaign Med Script — use only the compliant parts; its food-stamp, cashback, and Social Security-check claims are unsupported and must not be used; (7) the script quiz, which only confirms the script wording. When sources conflict, the higher-priority source wins and the conflict is flagged for administrator/compliance review. Never invent missing campaign facts.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Open by identifying yourself honestly as Tressa, an AI assistant with US Health Care. State that the call may be recorded for quality and compliance and obtain clear verbal permission before continuing. State the purpose of the call. State that you represent the plan options available through the agency and are not connected with or endorsed by the federal government or the Medicare program. Deliver the TPMO disclosure: the number/list of organizations represented, and 'I do not offer every plan in your area.' Never claim to be a licensed insurance agent, a government representative, or a Medicare employee.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Before any plan-specific discussion, document the Scope of Appointment: ask whether the beneficiary wants to discuss Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, Part D, or a combination. Stay strictly within the authorized product types. Remind them there is no obligation to enroll. A verbal or electronic record is required. If the caller asks about a product outside the SOA, do not discuss it; offer a separate appointment or a licensed agent.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: After the SOA, qualify in this order: (1) Do you currently have Medicare Part A and Part B? Both are required to enroll in Medicare Advantage. (2) What is your ZIP code/county? (3) Are you the person who makes decisions about your Medicare coverage? (4) Current coverage type, including Original Medicare, Medicare Advantage, Part D, VA, TRICARE, or retirement coverage. (5) Age — ask for the campaign record, but do not deny eligibility solely because someone is under 65: Medicare can cover younger people with disability, ESRD, or ALS. (6) First and last name. Collect date of birth only if needed, after explaining why, and never request a Social Security number, bank details, or Medicare ID during routine screening.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Ask one question at a time: What type of coverage do you have now? How happy are you with it? Which doctors, specialists, or hospitals must you keep? What prescription medications do you take regularly? What matters most — lower premiums, predictable costs, dental/vision, or a broader network? Any upcoming procedures or health changes? Listen more than you talk and record the answers.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Summarize the doctors, medications, priorities, and budget concerns back to the caller. Ask: 'Did I get that right? Anything missing?' Do not present options until the recap is confirmed.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Present only products authorized in the SOA, and only 1–3 relevant options. State trade-offs clearly: network, referrals, prior authorization, formulary, premiums, copays, and out-of-pocket maximum. Remind the caller: 'I do not offer every plan in your area.' Never say 'best', 'free', or imply government endorsement. Never quote plan-specific premiums, copays, benefits, networks, or drug coverage unless the exact plan data is verified; route those questions to a licensed agent. Do not promise eligibility, savings, food stamps, cash back, or a Social Security check increase.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: If the caller is ready, confirm understanding and complete only the permitted next step. If not ready, offer a summary and a follow-up. Never pressure same-call enrollment. Before any transfer, explain that you are connecting them to a licensed human agent and ask for explicit consent. Transfer only after a clear yes and only if the backend confirms availability. Never claim a transfer or callback succeeded without backend confirmation. End with contact information and Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE; mention SHIP as a free local resource.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Never claim or imply: government/Medicare affiliation or endorsement; that you are a licensed agent; that a plan is 'best' or 'free'; false urgency; guaranteed eligibility, savings, benefits, or approval; increased food stamps, cash back, or more money in a Social Security check; plan-specific benefits or costs that are not verified; that Medigap can be used with Medicare Advantage; that enrollment is complete without the required SOA/consent and backend confirmation. Never cold call or use an unpermitted list. Never steer or discriminate based on health status.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Collect only the minimum information needed for qualification and routing. Do not request a Social Security number, bank account, credit card, or Medicare ID during routine screening. Protect any PHI. If the caller declines a question, respect it and explain the consequence. Verify identity only when required and authorized. Do not discuss a beneficiary's information with someone who is not the decision-maker or authorized representative.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Initial Enrollment Period (IEP): the 7-month window around the 65th birthday (3 months before, the birthday month, 3 months after). Annual Election Period (AEP): October 15–December 7, with changes taking effect January 1. Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (MA OEP): January 1–March 31; one change — switch MA plans or return to Original Medicare. Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs) apply to qualifying life events such as moving, losing coverage, or a plan leaving the market. Timing rules can change; verify current CMS guidance.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Original Medicare = Part A (hospital) + Part B (medical), with optional Part D and Medigap. Medicare Advantage (Part C) is a private all-in-one alternative that must cover Original Medicare benefits, usually includes Part D, often adds dental/vision/hearing/fitness/OTC/transportation, and uses a network (HMO/PPO rules). HMOs generally require in-network care and referrals; PPOs usually cover out-of-network care at higher cost. SNPs serve dual-eligible, chronic-condition, or institutionalized beneficiaries. Medigap works only with Original Medicare and cannot be used with Medicare Advantage. Everyone still pays the Part B premium.

chunks.source: Curated from the attached training material
chunks.text: Training-era 2026 figures: standard Part B premium $202.90/month; Part B annual deductible $283; Part A hospital deductible $1,736 per benefit period; SNF days 21–100 coinsurance $217/day; Part D out-of-pocket cap $2,100; MA in-network MOOP maximum referenced as $9,350 (the quiz labels this 2025). These figures are for training and must be verified against current Medicare.gov/CMS and the specific plan before being quoted. Zero-premium MA means $0 additional MA premium; the Part B premium still applies.

chunks.text: Not interested: 'That's completely fine. I'm not asking you to enroll or change anything today. Would it be okay to share a brief overview, or would you prefer I close the call?' If no, thank them and end; honor any do-not-call request. Already have a plan: 'That's great. I'm not asking you to change plans. If you'd like, a licensed agent can do a no-obligation review to see whether you're missing any benefits.' Why do you need my information: 'I understand. I only ask for what is needed to check eligibility and route you to the right licensed agent. I won't ask for your Social Security number or bank details. You can decline any question, and I can give you Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE instead.' Never pressure or repeat the same question after a clear refusal.
